# meta

What the public library website and Danbyte's catalog sort, filter and show for one entry: its category, family, a one-line summary, lifecycle dates and links to vendor documents. Allowed on every entry: device overlays, module overlays, pluggables, rack types and rack kits. Only write what a source says; leave a key out rather than guess a date or a URL. Danbyte fills a device type's lifecycle fields from `lifecycle` and creates link Documents from `links`.

Schema: [`danbyte/schema/meta.schema.json`](../../schema/meta.schema.json) (danbyte-library/v1).

## Keys

| Key | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `category` | one of `switch`, `router`, `firewall`, `server`, `storage`, `access-point`, `wireless-controller`, `load-balancer`, `optical`, `console-server`, `pdu`, `ups`, `patch-panel`, `kvm`, `appliance`, `other`, `module`, `pluggable`, `rack`, `rack-kit` |  | The entry's category, from a closed list so the website's filters stay small. Device types use one of the hardware categories; module types use `module` (plus `module_kind`); pluggables use `pluggable`; rack types `rack`; rack kits `rack-kit`. |
| `module_kind` | one of `psu`, `fan`, `network-module`, `supervisor`, `line-card`, `stack-kit`, `other` |  | Module types only: what kind of module it is. |
| `roles` | list of string (pattern) |  | Free, short, lower-case words for what the hardware is used for. Suggested: access, distribution, core, campus, datacenter, edge, branch, industrial, poe, mgig, stackable, modular, spine, leaf, oob. |
| `family` | string |  | The vendor's product family, as the vendor names it. |
| `summary` | string |  | One plain sentence describing the hardware, no marketing. |
| `lifecycle` | [lifecycle](#lifecycle) |  | Lifecycle dates from the vendor's own notices. `source` is required as soon as any date is given. The catalog derives a state from them: `current`, `end-of-sale` or `end-of-support`. |
| `links` | list of [link](#link) |  | Vendor documents about the hardware. Danbyte creates one link Document per entry on the device type (its category from `kind`). |
| `sources` | list of [url](#url) |  | Anything else used for this entry: dimensions, ports, bays, LEDs, colours. |

## Definitions

### url

An http(s) URL, as found, without tracking parameters.

Type: string (pattern)

### date

A date as YYYY-MM-DD, or YYYY-MM when only the month is published.

Type: string (pattern)

Example:

```yaml
'2027-10-31'
```

### lifecycle

Lifecycle dates from the vendor's own notices. `source` is required as soon as any date is given. The catalog derives a state from them: `current`, `end-of-sale` or `end-of-support`.

| Key | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `release_date` | [date](#date) |  | First shipped / announced as available. |
| `end_of_sale` | [date](#date) |  | Last day it can be ordered. |
| `end_of_security_updates` | [date](#date) |  | Last day of security fixes (vulnerability support). |
| `end_of_support` | [date](#date) |  | Last day of support (last date of support / end of life). |
| `source` | [url](#url) |  | The EoL / EoS notice or page the dates come from. |

Example:

```yaml
release_date: 2017-06
end_of_sale: '2027-10-31'
end_of_support: '2032-10-31'
source: https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/products/eos-eol-notice.html
```

### link

One vendor document.

| Key | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | one of `datasheet`, `install-guide`, `config-guide`, `product-page`, `eol-notice`, `eol-listing`, `support`, `software`, `white-paper`, `other` | yes | What the document is. |
| `title` | string |  | The document's title as the vendor gives it. |
| `url` | [url](#url) | yes | An http(s) URL, as found, without tracking parameters. |

Example:

```yaml
kind: datasheet
title: Cisco Catalyst 9300 Series Switches Data Sheet
url: https://www.cisco.com/...
```
